prompt_en: An environmental editorial photograph of one adult woman in a pristine, sophisticated boutique tea tasting gallery, using the supplied portrait as the appearance and identity reference: preserve her oval face, dark brown eyes, softly shaped lips, and long wavy black hair. The gallery combines pale limestone, walnut cabinetry, glass, brushed stainless steel shelves and celadon ceramics. She wears an ivory knit top and charcoal tailored trousers. Standing beside the counter with both feet planted on the floor and her weight balanced, she sets a small celadon cup onto a saucer: her right thumb and fingers hold the cup on opposite sides, her right elbow stays beside her waist, and her left palm rests flat on the nearby counter edge. The cup base meets the saucer surface. Show her face, both connected arms, the hand-to-cup contact, and the counter-to-floor relationship in a three-quarter environmental view. Through the glass partition, a second row of walnut shelves remains visible while a faint reflection of the nearer window occupies the same pane. A large side window gives broad cool daylight, and a recessed warm shelf lamp lights the ceramic display. Matte limestone scatters that daylight softly, brushed steel catches a narrow directional highlight, and the celadon glaze carries a small bright reflection. The counter casts a grounded shadow on its plinth; the woman and ceramics share the same directional light. Frame her entire standing figure at eye level with a 40mm lens and enough floor beneath her feet to assess balance. Keep the upper steel shelf and partition legible within moderate depth of field. Pale wall-to-floor seams and the partition frame joints stay readable, while the walnut counter plinth sits securely on the floor and separates diffuse stone from reflective glass. Beside the pane at shoulder height, the brushed steel shelf shows a narrow silver edge highlight against the broad subdued limestone shading; the neighboring pane simultaneously transmits the rear shelves and reflects the window. The broad window produces gradual shadow transitions across her knit sleeves and nearby counter, while the cup-to-saucer and shoe-to-floor contact shadows remain localized and readable. These wall joints, counter supports, limestone, steel shelf, glass pane and softly lit woman occupy the same connected tea gallery.
